string-array.name: step_dev_details
string-array.item: 1. Open Settings, then About phone.
2. Open Software information (on Samsung, Xiaomi and others the Build number lives there).
3. Tap Build number 7 times in a row.
4. Enter your screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) if Android asks for it.
5. Wait for the message “You are now a developer”.
6. Go back to Settings, open System, then Developer options to confirm the new menu exists.

string-array.name: step_wifi_details
string-array.item: 1. Open Settings, then System, then Developer options.
2. Turn on Wireless debugging and confirm with Allow.
3. Stay on the Wireless debugging page.
4. Tap “Pair device with pairing code” to show the 6-digit code.
5. Leave this screen visible. You will type the code into Shizuku in the next steps.
Tip: after a reboot this switch turns off. Come back here and turn it on again.

string-array.name: step_install_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below to open the Shizuku page on the Play Store.
2. Install “Shizuku” by RikkaApps.
3. Return to X-KeepAlive. This step completes on its own once the package is found.

string-array.name: step_start_details
string-array.item: 1. Open Shizuku and tap Pairing, then “Start via Wireless debugging”.
2. Tap “Pair device with pairing code” inside Shizuku if it asks.
3. Type the 6-digit code shown on the Wireless debugging page.
4. Wait for “Pairing successful”, then go back in Shizuku and tap Start.
5. Return here. The status becomes “Shizuku is running”.
If pairing fails, turn Wireless debugging off and on again and request a fresh code.

string-array.name: step_start_legacy_details
string-array.item: 1. Install ADB on a computer and connect the phone with USB debugging enabled.
2. Open Shizuku and follow “Start via ADB”.
3. Return here once Shizuku reports it is running.

string-array.name: step_auth_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below.
2. In the Shizuku prompt, tap Allow (ideally “Allow all the time”).
3. Return here. The step completes when Shizuku reports permission granted.

string-array.name: step_usage_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below to open Usage access.
2. Find X-KeepAlive in the list and turn on “Permit usage access”.
3. Come back. The step completes automatically.

string-array.name: step_notif_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below.
2. Tap Allow on the system prompt.
3. The X-KeepAlive status notification stays visible while monitoring runs.

string-array.name: step_power_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below to open the battery settings.
2. Choose “Unrestricted” (on some phones: “Don’t optimize”).
3. Come back. This step completes on its own once Android reports it.

string-array.name: step_gamebatt_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap the button below to open the battery settings of an added game.
2. Choose “Unrestricted” for that game.
3. Repeat for every game you keep in the background.

string-array.name: step_apps_details
string-array.item: 1. Tap Open Home below.
2. Tap Add app and pick a game from the list.
3. Turn its switch on. Repeat for up to 4 apps.
4. Come back here. This step finishes when at least one switch is on.

string-array.name: step_service_details
string-array.item: 1. On Home, turn on the switch next to the “0/4” counter.
2. Accept the “Start monitoring?” prompt.
3. The status changes to “Background management active” once Shizuku confirms a policy.
